julia_customer: Hey team — streaming API disconnects intermittently when we call from Windows (corporate proxy). Request ID: req_0a1b2c3d
julia_customer: Repro steps: Windows 10, Powershell, curl.exe. Starts streaming then connection resets after ~18–22s.
julia_customer: curl command we used:
```
curl.exe --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses/stream?model=gpt-4o&prompt=hello"
```
gina_support: Thanks — can you paste the verbose curl output (-v) and confirm curl.exe version? Also include the x-request-id from the server response (if present). If you can run tcpdump or Wireshark around the failure window that helps. :mag:
julia_customer: curl 7.79.1 (Win64) — attached a small trace below. Server sent x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d-5ef just before the reset.
```
* Connected to api.redwood.example (52.12.34.56) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/responses/stream?... HTTP/1.1\r\n> Host: api.redwood.example\r\n> Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\r\n> Accept: text/event-stream\r\n>\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n< content-type: text/event-stream\r\n< x-request-id: 0a1b2c3d-5ef\r\n* Received 512 bytes chunk
... (streaming)
* Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
```
sam_eng: My guess: corporate proxy is timing out or rewriting chunked responses. Windows curl.exe uses WinHTTP by default which behaves differently with keep-alives and chunked transfer. Try forcing HTTP/1.1 and explicit Connection headers. Also try Accept-Encoding: identity to avoid proxy compression buffering.
sam_eng: Example Powershell-friendly command to try:
```
curl.exe -v --http1.1 --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Connection: keep-alive" -H "Accept-Encoding: identity" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses/stream?model=gpt-4o&prompt=hello"
```
matt_infra: If the proxy is doing TLS inspection it may buffer and then kill long-lived chunked streams. If user can run from WSL/Git-Bash (uses libcurl) that often works. Also capture netsh trace/WinDivert if possible.
gina_support: Please run our debug-collector (it zips curl -v output, OS info, and any packet capture). Upload link: https://internal.redwood/debug-upload?ticket=SUP-4123&req=0a1b2c3d-5ef :lock_with_ink_pen:
ci_bot: Auto-note: Escalation created SUP-4123 for req=0a1b2c3d-5ef, assigned eng-runtime.
julia_customer: Ran the http1.1 + Accept-Encoding: identity test — slightly better but still drops around 40s. Attached full -v output and a short packet capture (pcap). Upload link: https://uploads.internal/pcap123.pcap
sam_eng: Thanks. We'll try to repro behind a proxy. Next steps: eng-runtime will spin up a small proxy test harness that mimics chunked buffering and see if we can trigger same Reset. Also try curl.exe --raw in case WinHTTP is altering CRLFs.
gina_support: For the debug bundle checklist: include (1) curl -v output, (2) the exact curl command you ran, (3) OS + curl version, (4) pcap around failure, (5) server x-request-id, (6) whether WSL/Git-Bash changes behavior.
julia_customer: Uploads sent. Thx for quick help :pray:
sam_eng: Ack — we'll follow up in SUP-4123 with findings. Meanwhile, temporary workaround: run curl inside WSL or use our hosted SDK that uses streaming over persistent http2 connection which proxies handle differently. :+1:
